record.paper_title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Twisted geodesic flows near the zero section
record.original_question: Let M be a compact Riemannian manifold, let σ be a symplectic 2-form on M, and consider the twisted symplectic form ω = ω_0 + π^*σ on T^*M, where ω_0 is the standard symplectic form and π: T^*M → M is the cotangent-bundle projection. For the standard metric Hamiltonian H (the kinetic energy), is it true that some neighborhood of the zero section M \subset T^*M always has finite Hofer–Zehnder capacity, that almost all energy levels of H carry periodic orbits, and that every sufficiently low energy level carries a contractible periodic orbit?

evidence.quote: Denote by ω0 the standard symplectic form on T∗M and by π : T∗M → M the natural projection. The form ω = ω0 + π∗σ on T∗M is symplectic (a twisted symplectic structure). The flow of the standard metric Hamiltonian H (the kinetic energy) on (T∗M, ω) describes the motion of a charge on M in the magnetic field σ.

Conjecture 4.2. For every M and any symplectic form σ, a neighborhood of M in T∗M has finite Hofer–Zehnder capacity. Moreover, almost all levels of H carry periodic orbits. When σ is symplectic, every low energy level of H has a contractible periodic orbit.

artifact.category_tag: twisted cotangent bundles and magnetic flows
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made. Ginzburg–Gürel (Duke Math. J., 2004) established finiteness of the relative Hofer–Zehnder capacity near a symplectic submanifold and proved almost existence of periodic orbits on low energy levels for symplectic magnetic forms; subsequent work (e.g., Schlenk; Usher; Kerman; Ginzburg–Gürel 2009 on the Weinstein–Moser theorem) extended existence of contractible periodic orbits on low energy levels under rationality/sphericality assumptions on the magnetic form. Recent works (e.g., Benedetti–Kang, 2023, on Hofer–Zehnder capacity of magnetic disc tangent bundles) continue to refine the picture, but the full conjecture for arbitrary compact $M$ and arbitrary closed $\sigma$ is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Relative Hofer-Zehnder capacity and periodic orbits in twisted cotangent bundles
status_evidence.snippet: The proof of the relative almost existence theorem hinges on the notion of the relative Hofer-Zehnder capacity and on showing that this capacity of a small neighborhood of a symplectic submanifold is finite.
status_evidence.claim: Finiteness of relative HZ capacity and almost existence near symplectic submanifolds established by Ginzburg–Gürel.

status_evidence.title: Periodic Orbits of Twisted Geodesic Flows and the Weinstein–Moser Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of periodic orbits of a twisted geodesic flow on all low energy levels and in all dimensions whenever the magnetic field form is symplectic and spherically rational.
status_evidence.claim: Contractible low-energy periodic orbits proven under symplectic + spherically rational hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: Hofer–Zehnder capacity of magnetic disc tangent bundles over constant curvature surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Computes/bounds the Hofer–Zehnder capacity in magnetic settings; ongoing research.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to investigate the conjecture quantitatively, indicating it remains active.
